scope: Image pricing strategy, activated Stripe catalog, and plan-aware checkout for Creator, Studio, and MAX.

research.finding: A familiar ladder separates plans by explicit usage and privacy/concurrency terms; GALX must not copy unsupported modes or promises.
Plain-language usage balances and reset expectations are easier to compare than opaque job labels; GALX will add those only with enforceable accounting.
Stripe supports recurring Prices with lookup keys and an active flag; activation is safe only after the application validates plan keys, recurring terms, webhook delivery, and paid-price policy.

strategy.current_offer: Start free plus GALX Pro at the existing published $10/month contract.

guardrails: Products and Prices are active and have checkoutEnabled=true only after the backend and webhook checks passed.
No customers, subscriptions, invoices, payments, tax registrations, or application entitlements were created.
The old unused Pro $20 Price was archived and the lookup key now resolves to the published $10 contract.

The former MAX/Team $75 Price was archived only after the live subscription inventory showed zero active subscriptions; the stable private billing identity now resolves to the published $200 contract.
Private mode remains an owner-scoped product control, not a plan entitlement.
Higher usage, throughput, seats, roles, support, video, editing and priority are release gates, not current promises.
verification: The provisioning and activation commands use deterministic Product IDs, lookup keys, metadata and idempotency keys.
Live Stripe readback confirmed the Pro, Creator, Studio, and MAX Products and recurring Prices are active with the reviewed amounts.
The activation audit found no active consumer subscriptions, verified the production webhook and billing portal, and updated the private paid-price allowlist to four prices.
The production verification command observed zero active subscriptions and zero active Stripe Tax registrations; automatic tax remains disabled until registrations are confirmed.
No secret, customer data or webhook payload was recorded in this evidence.
limits: The paid tiers currently share the supported one-account Image Studio controls and fair-use boundary. MAX account sharing, seats, shared workspaces, priority, video, editing, and plan-specific monthly quotas are not implemented or advertised.
